title: Dynamic token scaling and chart legend collapse: Safari/Firefox/mobile QA triage
creator: Sofia Rivera
description: Background: During the most recent component sweep we received multiple reports of inconsistent density and layout regressions across Safari (iOS/macOS), Firefox, and Android WebView. Two classes of issues emerged: 1) dynamic token scaling math produces subpixel reflow that shifts button and table cell alignment at certain zoom/viewport combinations; 2) chart legend items collapse or overflow behind the canvas when the chart container is narrow or when RTL is enabled. Goals: triage, reproduce with deterministic test matrix, propose fixes that are low-risk for the upcoming patch release. Acceptance criteria: a) reproduce and document 3 deterministic repro cases (Safari mobile, Firefox desktop narrow width, Android WebView momentum scroll), b) ship a design + engineering mitigation plan with PRs referenced, c) add automated visual regression checks for the token scale edgecases and legend overflow behavior.
steps_to_reproduce: Repro A (iOS Safari): Open Dashboard > Reports > Dense table view on iPhone 14 simulator (Safari). Toggle compact density tokens to 'auto' and change font size (Settings > Accessibility > Larger Text). Observe 1-2px horizontal misalignment between action buttons and table cells in the first 3 rows.

Repro B (Firefox, desktop narrow): Open charts page in Firefox 118, resize window to 840px width, enable RTL locale. Chart legend items should wrap; observed behavior: legend collapses into a stacked list but the last item is hidden behind the chart canvas on initial render.

Repro C (Android WebView): In the mobile app using embedded WebView (Android 13), open a long table with sticky headers and momentum scrolling. Scroll quickly; header will detach or jump due to transform context + sticky interaction.

Repro D (Cross-browser token scaling): Using responsive token demo (Design Kit > Token Scale Playground), set base token scale to 0.875 and viewport width to 375px. Observe fractional pixel values in computed CSS variables (e.g., --space-md: 7.5px) causing blurry borders on 1px strokes in Safari.
Notes: All repros were validated against main branch commit hash ffbd23a. Repro steps captured in short screen recordings attached to links below.
observed_behaviors: Subpixel rounding in Safari leads to 1px misalignment on compact buttons and table cells at particular token scales.
Chart legend overflow: Firefox sometimes calculates flex-basis differently under RTL leading to items being painted under the canvas layer until a forced reflow occurs (resize or CSS change).
Sticky header reflow in Android WebView when parent container uses transform: translateZ(0) or has -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; header loses stickiness and jumps on momentum scroll.
Visual regression tests for token scaling do not currently cover odd-numbered viewport widths or accessibility font-scale combos.
proposed_fixes: Tokens: Switch runtime token scaler to snap values to whole pixels for spacing and borders. Implement a Math.round-based step for CSS variable generation in the build-time token bundler (Design system tokenizer). Add configurable 'pixelSnap' flag (default true) to avoid subpixel values for core spacing/border tokens.

Charts: Update legend layout to use a flex container with overflow-wrap: anywhere; fallback to a single-line scroll for very narrow widths. Also add a small right-padding spacer element to ensure the last legend item cannot overlap the canvas. Add RTL-specific test cases.

Sticky headers: Remove transform context from table wrapper (perform transform operations on inner scrollers only) or use will-change: top on sticky headers to improve WebKit handling. Add a guard in CSS that disables -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch for the table container in Android WebView when stickies are present.

QA/Automations: Add visual diff tests for the token playground across widths [320, 375, 414, 768] and font-scales [100%, 125%, 150%]. Add Percy/Chromatic scenarios for chart legend in RTL and narrow widths. Document repro cases in Confluence.
qa_checklist: Create deterministic Cypress fixtures that load the token demo and assert computed CSS variables are integers for spacing tokens when pixelSnap=true.
Record and attach device lab screenshots for iOS Safari (iPhone 12/14), Android WebView (Pixel 5/7), and Firefox desktop at 840px width.
Run visual diffs pre/post fix across the specified viewport and font-scale matrix.
Add unit test for token bundler to ensure pixel snapping does not impact font-size tokens used for accessibility.
Verify chart legend behavior in RTL locales and at 320px/360px/375px widths; ensure no overlap with canvas.
Smoke test sticky header behavior on Android WebView build with dev flags; confirm no header jumps under rapid scroll.
comments: 2025-03-10 Sofia Rivera: Initial triage — compiled repros from Design QA and two customer reports. Prioritized as P1 because button/table misalignment impacts perceived product polish in reporting flows.

2025-03-11 Liam Chen: Confirmed Safari repro on iOS simulator. Quick experiment: applying pixelRound() to spacing tokens in local build resolves alignment in 90% of sampled pages. Will open PR with toggle flag.

2025-03-12 Ava Martinez (Engineering): Noted potential ripple: rounding spacing may change total layout in tight card grids. Proposed adding safe guard: only snap tokens below 12px and keep larger ones fractional to preserve scale. Added ENG-6021 as dependency.

2025-03-13 Design review (Sofia + Priya Singh): Approved approach for token pixel snapping with conservative threshold; asked engineering to add automated visual diffs before merge. Also requested accessibility sign-off to ensure font scaling unaffected.

2025-03-14 Liam Chen: Opened token PR #3456 and chart legend PR #3472. Both include Percy snapshots. QA to validate mobile WebView stickiness separately; mobile eng owns final verification. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-6102.
